quotes: The coercivity ( H c ) decreased with increasing annealing temperature from 15 Oe for sample aged at 600 °C/15 h, exhibiting nanoscale phase separation, to 4 Oe for samples aged at 1000 °C/15 h, exhibiting a homogeneous undecomposed B2 matrix.
The M S of AlCoFeNi is substantially higher compared to that of the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy for both heat-treated conditions.

While the AlCoFeNi alloy exhibits a compositionally homogeneous single B2 phase on annealing at higher temperatures (1000 °C), it tends to decompose into a two-phase mixture of B2 + BCC on annealing at lower temperatures (600 °C).

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy. Intervention: Annealing temperature reduction from 1000 °C to 600 °C. Processing: Isothermal annealing for 15 h under argon. Test conditions: Comparison of 1000 °C vs 600 °C. Structure change: Transition from single B2 phase to early stage B2 + BCC phase separation with fine precipitates. Property change: Coercivity increased from 4.3 Oe to 14.5 Oe; Saturation magnetization decreased from 111.6 emu/g to 99.8 emu/g. Mechanism: Lower temperature induces phase separation which affects magnetic properties by increasing coercivity. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The coercivity ( H c ) decreased with increasing annealing temperature from 15 Oe for sample aged at 600 °C/15 h, exhibiting nanoscale phase separation, to 4 Oe for samples aged at 1000 °C/15 h, exhibiting a homogeneous undecomposed B2 matrix."

quotes: It is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity.
This is mainly due to the antiferromagnetic nature of Cr.
Addition of Cr strongly enhances the tendency of the B2 phase to decompose into a B2 + BCC mixture, as observed from the experimental results from the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. Intervention: Annealing at 1000 °C vs 600 °C. Processing: Annealing for 15 h under argon. Test conditions: 1000 °C vs 600 °C. Structure change: Coarse micron-scale decomposition at 1000 °C; refined multi-scale decomposition (nm to µm) at 600 °C. item.test_conditions: Predicted phase stability for AlCoFeNi at 1000 °C and 600 °C
item.structure_change: Predicted B2 + FCC at 1000 °C; B2 + BCC at 600 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Thermodynamic calculations rationalize experimental observations of phase stability
quotes: The experimentally observed microstructures and the implied phase stability were validated by thermodynamic calculations using the CALPHAD approach within the framework of the PANDAT software.
The predicted equilibrium phases for the AlCoFeNi alloy, on the extreme left of this isopleth, at 1000 °C consists of the B2 and FCC phases while at 600 °C consists of the B2 and BCC phases.
Our experimental investigations match very well with the thermodynamic predictions, except for the FCC phase predicted in AlCoFeNi alloy at 1000 °C.

Test conditions: Predicted phase stability for AlCoFeNi at 1000 °C and 600 °C. Structure change: Predicted B2 + FCC at 1000 °C; B2 + BCC at 600 °C. Property change: Not stated (model predicts phase stability). Mechanism: Thermodynamic calculations rationalize experimental observations of phase stability. Evidence: calculated. Quote: "The experimentally observed microstructures and the implied phase stability were validated by thermodynamic calculations using the CALPHAD approach within the framework of the PANDAT software."

item.structure_change: Predicted B2 + BCC + FCC at 1000 °C; B2 + BCC + sigma at 600 °C
item.attributed_mechanism: Positive enthalpy of mixing for Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, Ni-Cr systems drives phase separation
quotes: On the other hand, in the case of the AlCr0.5Co0.5FeNi alloy, which lies at the center of the isopleth, the equilibrium phases at 1000 °C are the B2, BCC and FCC phases while at 600 °C the equilibrium phases are the B2, BCC and sigma phases.
The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems.
The PANDAT computations also indicate that the B2 + BCC + FCC phase field, for this composition, extends to a very high temperature of ~1400 °C
